diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\mat{A} \in \R^{m \times n^d}$ be a matrix with the rows given by Kronecker products of $d$ random vectors in $\R^n$ with i.i.d. mean zero, variance one, sub-Gaussian entries.
whose coordinates are independent random variables that are bounded away from zero, $|( \mat{A}_i)_{kl}| > q > 0$ a.s.
Note that both $\tX$ and $\tY$ are rank $1$ tensors and their norms $\|\tX\|_F^2 , \|\tY\|^2_F > q^{2d}n^d$.
Such measurements do not have good RIP properties (recall Proposition~\ref{prop:db_friendly_trip})

issues.failure_explanation: The informal theorem states the no-trimming TensorRIP failure under the hypothesis of i.i.d. mean-zero variance-one sub-Gaussian entries. The only proof in the source (Proposition prop:db_friendly_trip) additionally requires the entries to be bounded away from zero almost surely ($|(\mat{A}_i)_{kl}| > q$), and its key step $\|\tX\|_F^2, \|\tY\|_F^2 > q^{2d}n^d$ a.s. uses exactly that; e.g., Gaussian entries (the ensemble used in the experiments, which invoke this proposition) are not bounded away from zero. The following remark only sketches an extension to spherical rows, so the stated generality is not established in the source.

failure_location.quote: However, if we do \emph{not} remove any rows, that is, we try to get a standard RIP guarantee for the set low-rank tensors, then we fail essentially with any nontrivial amount of compression: for any $\alpha > 0$, the probability of \eqref{eq:trim-rip} with $\mat{A}^\vy = \mat{A}$ goes to zero for any $m < n^{d(1 - \alpha)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend the proof of Proposition prop:db_friendly_trip to general sub-Gaussian entries by replacing the almost-sure lower bounds with high-probability ones ($\|\va\|_2^2 \ge n/2$ with probability $1 - e^{-cn}$, adding a negligible term to the failure probability), or restrict the informal theorem's hypothesis to the ensembles actually covered.
issues.overall_effect: The headline negative claim of thm:main-informal, and its application to Gaussian face-splitting measurements in Section 5, are not covered by the formal result; the impossibility statement is proved only for a restricted measurement class.
issues.title: RIP-failure of face-splitting measurements asserted for all sub-Gaussian ensembles but proved only for entries bounded away from zero
issues.why_classification: The extension is a routine local modification of the existing proof using standard lower-tail bounds; the claim, its scope, and the paper's message survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, there exist constants $C,c \in \R^+$ such that for any $\alpha \geq 4e^{-cp}$, for $k_1 = 0$ and $k_2 = \ln(8/\alpha)$,
The desired result follows by the union bound argument.
we consider their embedding with respect to the data-driven row trimming of $\mat{A}^{\vx}_k$ with $k = \ln(8n^\phi)$

issues.failure_explanation: In the cited trimmed-mean theorem, the trimming level and the failure probability are tied: trimming $k_2 = \ln(8/\alpha')$ rows yields failure $\alpha'$ per point. The proof of Lemma lem:jl_trimming unions over $p$ tensors, so the per-point failure must be $\alpha' = \alpha/p$, which forces $k = \ln(8p/\alpha)$ — exactly matching the stated sample complexity $m \ge C^d\delta^{-2}\ln(4p/\alpha)$ — not the stated $k = \ln(8/\alpha)$. With the stated $k$, the conclusion holds only with probability $1 - p\alpha$. (The stated side condition $\alpha \ge 4e^{-cp}$ also uses the wrong variable; the trimmed-mean theorem requires the per-point failure to be at least $4e^{-cm}$.) Consequently Theorem theorem:trim_trip, which applies the lemma over a net of size $|\mathcal{N}|$ with $\alpha = n^{-\phi}$, needs $k = \ln(8|\mathcal{N}|n^{\phi}) = \Theta((r^d+dnr)\ln(n^{d/2}(d+1)/\delta))$ — a $\Theta(\delta^2)$-fraction of the $m$ rows — rather than the stated $k = \ln(8n^\phi)$.

failure_location.quote:
we consider their embedding with respect to the data-driven row trimming of $\mat{A}^{\vx_i}_k$ with $\vx_i = \algoname{Vec}(\tX_i)$ and $k = \ln(8/\alpha)$, 
 and $\alpha \geq 4e^{-cp}$. If $m \geq C^d \delta^{-2}\ln(4p/\alpha)$, then
$$\left|\left\|\mat{A}_{k}^{\vx_i} \vx_i\right\|_2^2 - \left\|\vx_i\right\|_2^2\right| \leq \delta  \left\|\vx_i\right\|_2^2\text{ for all } i \in [p]$$
with probability at least $1 - \alpha$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Lemma lem:jl_trimming with $k = \ln(8p/\alpha)$ and propagate the larger trimming level $k = \ln(8|\mathcal{N}|n^\phi)$ to Theorem theorem:trim_trip, thm:main-informal, and the $m_{trim}$ guidance; the sample complexity $m$ and the remainder of the proofs are unchanged, and $k < m$ still holds for $\delta$ small.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:jl_trimming is unproven as stated; Theorem theorem:trim_trip's quantitative trimming level, the informal theorem's 'version of $\mat{A}$ without $\ln(8n^\phi)$ rows', and the algorithmic guidance '$m_{trim} \approx \ln(8n)$' in rem:trimtiht-discussion all become unsupported at their stated levels.
issues.title: Trimming level k = ln(8/alpha) in Lemma lem:jl_trimming ignores the union bound over the p points
issues.why_classification: The repair preserves the trimmed-RIP guarantee and the sample complexity, but materially worsens the advertised trimming level from polylogarithmic in $n$ to a constant ($\delta^2$) fraction of the rows; a recognizably comparable result survives, so it is more than a local fix yet not a loss of the result or its regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, note that (e.g., \cite[Lemma 2]{zhang2018median}), $\|\vu_{(k)} - \vv_{(k)}\| \leq \|\vu-\vv\|_\infty$ for any two vectors $\vu$ and $\vv$ and their $k$-th order statistics.

Without loss of generality, we can also assume that the rows $\{\va^\vx_i\}$ and $\{\va^{\hat{\vx}}_i\}$ of $\mat{A}^{\vx}$ and $\mat{A}^{\hat\vx}$ respectively have been reordered such that,
    $$ |\mat{a}^{\vx}_1{\vx}| \leq |\mat{a}^{\vx}_2{\vx}| \le \dots \le |\mat{a}^{\vx}_{m-k}{\vx}| \text{ and } |\mat{a}^{\hat{\vx}}_1{\hat{\vx}}| \leq 
    |\mat{a}^{\hat\vx}_2{\vx}|_2 \le \dots \le |\mat{a}^{\hat\vx}_{m-k}{\hat\vx}| .$$

issues.failure_explanation: The $j$-th entries of the two trimmed vectors are the $j$-th smallest-magnitude signed inner products with respect to two different vectors $\vx, \hat\vx$ (different retained index sets and orderings). The cited order-statistic Lipschitz property holds for value-sorted (or magnitude-sorted absolute) sequences, not for signed sequences sorted by magnitude. Counterexample: $\vu = (5, -5.1)$, $\vv = (5.1, -5)$, keep the single smallest-magnitude entry: $\vu' = (5)$, $\vv' = (-5)$, so $\|\vu' - \vv'\|_2^2 = 100$ while $m\|\vu - \vv\|_\infty^2 = 2(0.2)^2 = 0.08$. Such near-tied magnitudes with opposite signs occur generically among the $m$ inner products $\{\va_i^\intercal\vx\}$. Hence the displayed inequality is false, and the off-net perturbation control (with $\varepsilon = \delta n^{-d/2}/3$) that drives the rest of the proof is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the vector-valued perturbation bound by a scalar one: use the valid Lipschitz property of magnitude order statistics, $||u|_{[j]} - |v|_{[j]}| \le \|\mat{A}(\vx-\hat\vx)\|_\infty$, to get $\big|\|\mat{A}^\vx\vx\|_2^2 - \|\mat{A}^{\hat\vx}\hat\vx\|_2^2\big| \le \sqrt{m}\,\delta_\infty(\|\mat{A}^\vx\vx\|_2 + \|\mat{A}^{\hat\vx}\hat\vx\|_2)$, and close a self-bounding argument on $S = \sup_{\vx\in\mathcal{S}}\|\mat{A}^\vx\vx\|_2^2$ (giving $S \le 1 + O(\delta)$ and the same conclusion with the same $\varepsilon = \delta n^{-d/2}/3$ and the same $m$).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the paper's central positive result (Theorem theorem:trim_trip, trimmed TensorRIP for face-splitting measurements) is incomplete; the informal restatement thm:main-informal and the TrimTIHT motivation in rem:trimtiht-discussion (high-probability control of $|1-\Delta_t|$ via trimming) rely on it.
issues.title: Net-continuity step in Theorem theorem:trim_trip uses a false Lipschitz inequality for magnitude-trimmed vectors
issues.why_classification: The key inequality of the main theorem's proof is false, so a replacement argument is required; a contained (but nontrivial) new perturbation lemma with a bootstrap step repairs it with no change to the statement, rates, or advertised scope — more than a routine local fix, but no new global architecture and no loss of the result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F 
\leq \left( 2\sqrt{ 1 - (2 - \mu_t\rho_t )\mu_t\Delta_t  }+\sqrt{( 2\xi_t + \xi_t^2)}\left(1 + \mu_t \|\mat{A}_t\|_{2} \sqrt{\Delta_t}\right) \right) \|\tR^t\|_F,
which concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main_path}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only the per-iteration relation $\|\tR^{s+1}\|_F \le \alpha_s\|\tR^s\|_F$, where $\alpha_s$ is the bracket evaluated with the iteration-dependent quantities $\mu_s, \rho_s, \Delta_s, \xi_s, \|\mat{A}_s\|_2$. Since these vary across iterations, iterating yields $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F \le \big(\prod_{s=0}^{t}\alpha_s\big)\|\tR^0\|_F$, not $\alpha_t^{t+1}\|\tR^0\|_F$; the stated powered closed form is not implied and is false in general (e.g., when the final factor is smaller than earlier ones).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the conclusion as $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F \le \big(\prod_{s=0}^{t}\alpha_s\big)\|\tR^0\|_F$ (or with $(\max_s\alpha_s)^{t+1}$), or state the per-iteration bound only.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed convergence bound (eqn:conv_path) is not established as written; the per-step discussion in rem:trimtiht-discussion (including eqn:conv_path_err) is unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem thm:main_path states the error bound with the time-t factor raised to power t+1, but the proof only yields the per-step recurrence
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and preserves the theorem's content and all downstream per-step analysis; no new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The simplification requires $\sqrt{2\xi_t + \xi_t^2}(1 + \mu_t\|\mat{A}_t\|_2\sqrt{\Delta_t}) \le |1-\mu_t\Delta_t|$, i.e., $2\xi_t + \xi_t^2 \le X^2$ with $X = |1-\mu_t\Delta_t|/(1+\mu_t\|\mat{A}_t\|_2\sqrt{\Delta_t})$. The assumed bound $\xi_t \le \frac{16}{17}X^2$ gives only $2\xi_t + \xi_t^2 \le \frac{32}{17}X^2 + \frac{256}{289}X^4$, and $\frac{32}{17} > 1$: the saturating admissible choice $\xi_t = \frac{16}{17}X^2$ makes the actual noise term $\sqrt{2\xi_t+\xi_t^2}(1+\ldots) \ge \sqrt{32/17}\,|1-\mu_t\Delta_t| \approx 1.37|1-\mu_t\Delta_t|$, which exceeds the $|1-\mu_t\Delta_t|$ term in (eqn:conv_path_err). So the claimed simplification is false under the stated assumption; the constant must be small enough (e.g., $\le 1/4$) to ensure $2\xi_t+\xi_t^2 \le X^2$, or the assumption must be placed on $2\xi_t+\xi_t^2$ directly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the assumption on $\xi_t$ by replacing the constant $16/17$ with a constant $\le 1/2$ (e.g., $1/4$), or equivalently assume the bound on $2\xi_t + \xi_t^2$ directly.
issues.overall_effect: The simplified per-step rate (eqn:conv_path_err) is not valid under the stated thresholding-accuracy assumption; the subsequent 'Connection to TensorRIP' discussion (convergence for $\delta < 0.106$) uses only the form of (eqn:conv_path_err) and survives once the constant is corrected.
issues.title: The stated xi_t assumption (constant 16/17) does not imply the simplified rate (eqn:conv_path_err)
issues.why_classification: A one-constant correction restores the claim; the main theorem and all qualitative conclusions are unchanged.
